10041483:
Testimony of Michael R. Scott, President Professional Fire Fighters of Maine
LD 993 An Act to Require First Responder Training for Mental Health Crisis and Critical Incident Stress Recognition
Good morning, Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus, and distinguished members of the Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety.
My name is Michael Scott, and I am the President of the Professional Fire Fighters of Maine. I appreciate the opportunity to provide testimony today regarding LD 993, An Act to Require First Responder Training for Mental Health Crisis and Critical Incident Stress Recognition. I represent over 1,200 members, including career firefighters, paramedics, EMTs, and dispatchers. For more than 75 years, the Professional Fire Fighters of Maine (PFFMaine) have been committed to enhancing the health and safety of firefighters.
I stand before you today to voice our unwavering support for LD 993, an act that seeks to establish and recognize essential training for our first responders in mental health crisis management, critical incident stress recognition, and peer team support initiatives. As we navigate an era marked by increasing demands on our emergency services--characterized by significant emotional and psychological strain--it is imperative that we equip our first responders with the knowledge and skills necessary to recognize and respond effectively to mental health crises.
First responders, including firefighters, police officers, and emergency medical personnel, are often on the front lines of crises that extend beyond physical emergencies. The nature of our work exposes us to traumatic events, high-stress scenarios, and the difficult realities of human suffering. Studies indicate that first responders experience higher rates of anxiety, depression, and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) compared to the general population. Acknowledging this reality is the first step toward safeguarding the mental well-being of our heroic personnel.

Despite these challenges, and although the situation is improving, there remains a stigma surrounding mental health discussions within the first responder community. This stigma can deter individuals from seeking help and may exacerbate the psychological toll that the job takes. LD 993 is a vital initiative aimed at breaking this cycle and fostering a supportive environment where mental health is prioritized alongside physical health.
The demand for mental health crisis training cannot be overstated. Emergency responders must be equipped not only to address physical injuries but also to understand, recognize, and respond to the mental health needs of the individuals they serve. The proposed legislation will provide standardized training consistent with industry best practices, ensuring that all first responders across Maine receive a baseline of knowledge and skills that align with recognized behavioral health programs.
One of the benchmarks for such training can be found in the programs developed by the International Association of Fire Fighters (IAFF) and its Center of Excellence. The IAFF's and PFFMaine's Behavioral Health Programs have emerged as a gold standard within the industry, offering structured, evidence-based training that addresses the nuances of mental health crises faced by first responders.
LD 993 seeks to implement a similar approach in Maine, emphasizing not just theoretical understanding but also practical applications. This training will cover critical incident stress recognition, coping mechanisms, and de-escalation techniques, providing our first responders with a toolkit to navigate mental health scenarios proficiently.
By advocating for LD 993, we encourage a cultural shift within our community--a shift that normalizes conversations around mental health, promotes proactive engagement, and fosters resilience among our personnel. Education and training will empower first responders to address the immediate needs of crisis situations while also recognizing their limits and the importance of seeking help when needed.
Enacting LD 993 will create an environment where mental health is treated with the same urgency and care as physical health. This aligns perfectly with our values as firefighters: to protect and serve not only the communities we respond to but also each other. By strengthening our approach to mental health, we can embody the supportive family that first responder communities often declare themselves to be.
Establishing consistent training standards and standards of care across all first responder agencies in Maine is crucial. Such uniformity ensures that every responding member, regardless of their location or department, operates from the same playbook. This consistency leads to improved outcomes for both responders and the communities they serve.
When first responders have a shared understanding of mental health crisis protocols, it ensures better collaboration during joint responses to critical incidents. This teamwork is not only beneficial on the front lines but also builds stronger inter-departmental relationships and fosters a community that looks out for one another.

While we recognize the undeniable benefits of LD 993, we must also acknowledge the challenges that lie ahead. Implementing comprehensive training requires funding, resources, and a commitment from leadership at all levels. This is where the Professional Fire Fighters of Maine can make a significant impact. By rallying our collective support behind this initiative, we can help secure the necessary resources to prioritize mental health training and access to behavioral health resources in our state.
Support for LD 993 must be championed at the grassroots level--starting with our elected officials, all municipalities, and all fire/police departments, as well as other public safety entities within our firehouses, through community outreach and in public forums. Now more than ever, our voices must unite to advocate for the mental health of our first responders and the communities we serve.
Maine's LD 993 represents an essential step toward safeguarding our first responders' mental health and well-being while fostering a more resilient and effective emergency response framework. As the Professional Fire Fighters of Maine, our support for this legislation can change lives--both for those on the front lines and the communities they serve.
In closing, we are asking all of you, along with other members of the House and Senate and our Governor, to join us in supporting the passage and implementation of LD 993. Together, we can cultivate a culture that emphasizes the importance of mental health training, providing our first responders with the tools they need to recognize and respond to mental health crises effectively. By committing to this cause, we not only honor our calling but also ensure that we are prepared to meet the challenges of today and tomorrow with compassion, understanding, and readiness.
Thank you for considering this crucial initiative and for your steadfast commitment to the wellbeing of all Maine's first responders. Your support for LD 993 is not just a vote for legislation; it is a vote for the mental health and future of our community.
Sincerely,
Michael
Michael Scott, President Professional Fire Fighters of Maine
April 2, 2025

Good afternoon, Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus and esteemed members of the Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety.
My name is Simonne Maline. I am the Executive Director for the Consumer Council System of Maine (CCSM). I am here today on behalf of the CCSM to testify in support of LD 993.
The Consumer Council System of Maine is a public instrumentality written into State Statute by the Maine Legislature to serve in an advisory capacity and to provide legislators with guidance and advice regarding the delivery of effective and appropriate adult mental health services from those served by them.
Maine is in the process of a needed reformation of its crisis system, prioritizing trauma-informed care that ensures individuals experiencing a mental health crisis receive the appropriate support. This reform represents a critical shift away from criminal justice involvement toward a person-centered approach. We want to extend gratitude to the first responders who have continuously and graciously provided care to those in crisis prior to this system reform. CCSM understands the psychological toll and emotional fatigue that is associated with responding to traumatic situations and believes this training would provide necessary support for first responders.
The development of peer-led crisis services is vital; yet first responders will continue to often be the first touch for individuals in crisis. Ensuring these first responders receive thorough and meaningful mental health crisis training is an essential step in reducing unnecessary use of force, promoting deescalation, and fostering connections to appropriate services. By including training on stress recognition and coping strategies, LD 993 acknowledges the importance of first responder well-being in maintaining a healthy and effective emergency response system.
CCSM believes that a trauma-informed co-response team is key to an effective crisis response system. While we continue to advocate for expanded co-response teams, we recognize the necessity of comprehensive mental health training for first responders, who will inevitably encounter individuals in crisis. We urge the committee to vote ought to pass on LD 993 to equip Maine's first responders with the training needed to support individuals facing mental health challenges with compassion and respect while also ensuring they have access to the necessary support for managing stress and trauma.
Sincerely,

Simonne M. Maline

Senator Pinny Beebe-Center, Senate Chair Representative Tavis Hasenfus, House Chair Joint Standing Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety c/o Legislative Information Office 100 State House Station Augusta, ME 04333
RE: LD 993 - "An Act to Require First Responder Training for Mental Health Crisis and Critical Incident Stress Recognition"
Dear Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus, and Members of the Committee,
I respectfully request that the Committee vote Ought Not to Pass on LD 993, "An Act to Require First Responder Training for Mental Health Crisis and Critical Incident Stress Recognition."
As the sponsor of this bill, I introduced LD 993 to address a real and growing need: ensuring our first responders have access to consistent training that helps them recognize and manage mental health crises and critical incident stress -- for themselves and for the people they serve.
However, over the course of the session and in conversation with stakeholders, it has become clear that this proposal requires further refinement to ensure it is workable, effective, and appropriately aligned with existing supports and programs.
I remain fully committed to this policy goal and plan to work collaboratively with the Department of Public Safety, peer support teams, and mental health professionals to strengthen the concept and bring forward an improved version in the future.
Thank you for your consideration, and for your continued efforts to support the safety and well-being of Maine's first responders and communities.
Sincerely,
AA--
Tim Nangle State Senator, Senate District 26 Representing Casco, Frye Island, Raymond, Windham, and part of Westbrook
